label: verify-t3-lumen-deep

claims.claim: In MDCK spheroids the lumen is non-spherical (sphericity about 0.3-0.7) with a large concave fraction (10 to over 50 percent of surface), unlike the nearly spherical outer surface.
claims.source_says: The sphericity of lumens ranged from Ψ ~ 0.70 to very far from spherical (Ψ ~ 0.3)... percent of the total lumen surface area with negative mean curvature varied from 10% to over 50%... basal surfaces... close to 1 and 0%
claims.note: All three parts match the Europe PMC full text of Vasquez 2021 (PMC8460836).

claims.claim: Claudin-knockout MDCK cysts form lumens of unchanged solidity, which Vasquez et al. take to mean pressure alone is not the main shape determinant; apical size per cell and cell number are.
claims.source_says: Cldn-qKO cells formed lumens whose solidity did not differ from wildtype to a significant degree... pressure alone is not the primary driver for determining lumen shape and size... apical domain size, rather than pressure or cortical tension, might play a dominant role
claims.note: Cell number is a second factor in the model (solidity rises with size), which is consistent with the claim.

claims.claim: The pressure role is contested: an independent lab measures about 65 Pa in MDCK cysts and argues lumen dynamics are pressure-determined, while Vasquez et al. never measure pressure (their p is dimensionless).
claims.source_says: Hydrostatic pressure measurements show an average of 65 Pa in MDCK cysts and close to 0 Pa in epiblasts.
claims.note: Lu 2025 text has the 65 Pa figure; no pascal value appears in Vasquez; I did not assess how strongly Lu argues pressure-determined dynamics, but the title compares with and without pressure.

claims.claim: Under law set 1.8.1 the only applicable accepted law is physiology-laplace; the cell-geometry and Thompson-library lumen theorems cited earlier are not in the 1.8.1 repo lean/ directory, only in the older leanbio copy.
claims.source_says: For a thin-walled sphere the wall stress is P r / (2 t) and for a cylinder P r / t; ... a wall that holds at most sigma_max limits the pressure to 2 sigma_max t / r
claims.note: Lawset 1.8.1 has 59 laws, physiology-laplace is accepted, and grep for tripleJunction/ThompsonLaws/CellGeometry in lean/ found nothing; I did not open the leanbio copy, and 'only applicable' is a judgment from law IDs (no other mentions lumen or Laplace).

overall: Claims 1-3 reproduce from the published Vasquez 2021 and Lu 2025 full texts. Claim 4 is confirmed on the 1.8.1 side (59 laws, physiology-laplace present, no CellGeometry/ThompsonLaws in lean/). I did not check the leanbio side or that physiology-laplace is the only applicable law, so it is partly.
